headline: Train derails in Normandy, leaving 44 people hurt

sources.title: Train derails in France, injuring 44 people
Un train deraille en Seine-Maritime, 44 blesses dont une femme dans un etat grave

chunks.text: A [[regional]] train {{came off}} the rails in Normandy, in northern France, on Friday evening, September 11. The train had {{set out}} from Rouen and was traveling to Caen. It [[derailed]] near Cléon, in the Seine-Maritime area, at about 7:30 pm. There were 186 passengers [[on board]]. Forty-four people were hurt, roughly one passenger in four. One of them, an 18-year-old woman, was taken to the hospital in [[critical condition]]. The accident happened at the start of the weekend.

verbs.correct: To become separated from a surface
verbs.wrong: To visit a place for a short time
verbs.why: A lid can come off a jar if you twist it hard, and a button may come off a coat that is too tight. The train came off the rails near Cléon on Friday evening with 186 passengers on board.

verbs.correct: To begin a trip or journey
verbs.wrong: To keep something for later use
verbs.why: A family may set out for the beach before sunrise, and a delivery driver sets out on his route at seven. The train had set out from Rouen and was traveling to Caen when it derailed.

chunks.text: After the accident, [[investigators]] found a piece of [[rail]] lying on the [[track]]. The [[public prosecutor]] in Rouen {{pointed out}} that the reason it was there is unknown and still has to be [[established]]. Investigators are {{looking into}} the [[possibility]] that someone put it there [[deliberately]]. They have not {{ruled out}} that idea, but nobody has [[confirmed]] it either. For now, the case remains open, and no cause has been announced.

verbs.correct: To tell people about a certain fact
verbs.wrong: To delay something until a later time
verbs.why: A guide may point out that the museum closes at five, and a friend can point out that you left your keys on the table. The public prosecutor in Rouen pointed out that the reason the rail was there is still unknown.

verbs.wrong: To take care of someone or a place
verbs.why: A bank will look into a strange charge on your card, and a school may look into a complaint about a bus driver. Investigators are looking into the possibility that someone put the piece of rail on the track deliberately.

verbs.correct: To decide that something is not possible
verbs.wrong: To question a person about an event
verbs.why: A doctor can rule out a broken bone after an X-ray, and a coach may rule out playing an injured star this week. Investigators have not ruled out the idea that the rail was placed on purpose, but nobody has confirmed it.

chunks.text: The driver was tested for alcohol and drugs, and both tests {{came out}} [[negative]]. The national rail company, which runs the line, has also {{set up}} its own [[internal]] investigation. In the hours after the accident, [[rail services]] were {{shut down}} between Rouen and Caen, and between Caen and Le Havre. Trains [[in both directions]] were {{held up}} for the rest of the evening. [[Travelers]] on those lines had to wait or change their plans.

verbs.correct: To end with a certain result
verbs.wrong: To become sick with an illness
verbs.why: A blood test can come out normal, and a vote may come out in favor of a new park. The driver's tests for alcohol and drugs came out negative.

verbs.wrong: To cause a loud alarm to sound
verbs.why: A city can set up a hotline after a storm, and two friends may set up a small business selling bread. The national rail company set up its own internal investigation after the derailment.

verbs.correct: To stop a service from running
verbs.wrong: To keep someone from taking part
verbs.why: A factory may shut down for two weeks in August, and a city can shut down the subway during a storm. Rail services between Rouen and Caen, and between Caen and Le Havre, were shut down after the accident.

verbs.wrong: To choose not to do something yet
verbs.why: Heavy traffic can hold up a bus for an hour, and a missing form may hold up a visa for weeks. Trains in both directions were held up for the rest of Friday evening.

chunks.text: By Saturday morning, [[traffic]] had {{started up}} again on both routes. The bigger question, however, has not been answered. Investigators still need to {{clear up}} why a piece of rail was lying on the track, and whether anyone put it there. Nobody has confirmed that it was done [[on purpose]]. The rail company's own internal investigation is also [[under way]]. The public prosecutor has said only that the reason must be established, and the investigation is still {{going on}}.

verbs.why: An engine may start up on the second try, and the buses start up again at five in the morning. Rail traffic started up again on both routes by Saturday morning.

verbs.correct: To find the answer to a question
verbs.why: A quick call can clear up a mix-up about a date, and one email may clear up confusion over a price. Investigators still need to clear up why a piece of rail was lying on the track.

verbs.wrong: To make a sudden loud noise
verbs.why: A meeting can go on for three hours, and a party may go on until midnight. The investigation into the derailment is still going on, and no cause has been announced.

mainIdea.s: A regional train derailed near Cléon in Normandy, and 44 people were hurt. Investigators found a piece of rail on the track and are looking into why it was there.
mainIdea.why: The train came off the rails on Friday evening with 186 passengers on board. The reason the piece of rail was on the track is unknown, and the case is still open.

mainIdea.s: A regional train derailed near Cléon in Normandy, and 44 people were hurt. Investigators have confirmed that someone placed a piece of rail on the track on purpose.
mainIdea.why: Close, but nobody has confirmed that. Investigators are looking into the possibility, and they have not ruled it out either.

mainIdea.s: A regional train hit a car at a crossing near Cléon in Normandy, and 44 people were hurt. The driver was arrested after he failed his tests for alcohol and drugs.
mainIdea.why: No car was involved, and the train came off the rails after a piece of rail was found on the track. The driver's tests came out negative.

tf.s: The train came off the rails near Cléon on Friday evening.
tf.why: It derailed near Cléon, in the Seine-Maritime area, at about 7:30 pm on Friday, September 11. The train had set out from Rouen and was traveling to Caen.

tf.s: The train had set out from Caen and was on its way to Rouen.
tf.why: It set out from Rouen and was traveling to Caen. The derailment happened near Cléon, in the Seine-Maritime area.

tf.s: The driver's tests for alcohol and drugs came out negative.
tf.why: The driver was tested after the accident, and both results came out negative. The reason for the derailment is still unknown.

tf.s: Investigators have ruled out the idea that someone put the rail on the track on purpose.
tf.why: Investigators are looking into that possibility and have not ruled it out. Nobody has confirmed it either, and the case remains open.

tf.s: Rail traffic between Rouen and Caen had started up again by Saturday morning.
tf.why: Services on that route and between Caen and Le Havre were shut down after the accident. Traffic started up again on both routes by Saturday morning.

tf.s: The national rail company has not set up an investigation of its own.
tf.why: The company set up its own internal investigation after the derailment. It is under way alongside the public prosecutor's work.
